subject: Clarify billing for mixed long-prefetch + microcall pattern
messages:
From: Beth Lang <beth@quantifyhealth.com>
To: markus_klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement <procurement@quantifyhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Metering question — prefetch + many microcalls

Hi Markus,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We ran an internal spike and hit a usage pattern I wanted to raise before we get to contract: our ingestion pipeline does a large prefetch per patient (context ~12k tokens) once every 6 hours, and then the app issues hundreds of tiny microcalls (5–30 tokens) for event-driven scoring and alerts. The engineering team is worried about how those two patterns will be billed together — specifically:

- Is the 12k prefetch treated as a single context bucket charged once, or will subsequent microcalls be charged against that same bucket?
- Do you round microcalls up to the billing quantum? If so, that could materially increase our token count.
- Any minimums or floors we should expect for microcall-heavy traffic?

Attached a small sample (usage-sample.csv) and a draft SOW (SOW-draft.pdf). We’d appreciate a clear example calculation we can show our finance team. Also, we’re evaluating a 12-month committed package — would that change rounding/minimums behavior or enable a discounted rounding policy?

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if easier.

— Beth
Beth Lang
Head of Product
QuantifyHealth
From: markus_klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Beth Lang <beth@quantifyhealth.com>
Cc: kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, tessa_morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 11:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Metering question — prefetch + many microcalls

Beth — thanks for the concrete sample and the SOW. High level answers up-front, then I’ll add a worked example: 

1) Prefetch vs microcalls: We treat each request independently for token accounting, but we also apply prefix/KV cache reuse when a subsequent request can reuse cached KV entries from a recent prefetch. In practice:
   - The initial 12k prefetch will be billed for the tokens consumed by that call.
   - If microcalls can reuse the KV cache (same conversation key and within the active cache TTL), they typically only incur the incremental tokens (the microcall prompt + generation).

2) Rounding/quantum: Our billing quantum is 16 tokens for the model family in your SOW. We round up per-request token usage to that quantum when calculating invoice line items. That does mean a 5-token microcall becomes charged as 16 tokens unless you enable batching or a microcall aggregation policy.

3) Minimums/floors: For committed contracts (12-month), we can offer:
   - Reduced quantum for microcall aggregation (example: down to 8-token quantum for endpoints with >500k microcalls/month)
   - A monthly minimum (commit) with true-up; we can apply smoothing credits for bursty microcall patterns on a quarterly true-up.

Worked example (from your sample):
- One prefetch call: 12,000 tokens -> billed as 12,000 (no rounding impact on large calls).
- 1,200 microcalls at 7 tokens average -> round up to 16 per call -> 1,200 * 16 = 19,200 tokens billed (vs. 8,400 raw).

Net billed tokens for that window = 31,200. With a commitment discount (20% commit) + microcall-quantum reduction to 8 tokens, billed microcalls would be 1,200 * 8 = 9,600. Net billed tokens ~21,600 (before true-up credits).

Next steps: Kimberly — can you confirm the model family and exact quantum options for QH-2026-087 and confirm whether KV cache TTL for their integration is currently under 6 hours? Tessa — please add a short pilot concession we can offer in writing (2 months of microcall quantum set to 8 tokens) and the eligibility criteria.

If helpful, we can produce a one-page calculation and add it to the SOW. Happy to jump on a 30-min call with Beth and procurement tomorrow afternoon.

— Markus
Markus Klein
Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
From: kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 13:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Metering question — prefetch + many microcalls

Thanks Markus and Beth — a couple clarifications from the product side to avoid surprises: 

- Cache behavior: The runtime's KV cache TTL is 2 hours by default for private deployments and 4 hours for hosted. We can extend cache TTL for your Dedicated/Dual-tenant setup to 6 hours as part of onboarding, which should allow most microcalls to hit the cached KV for the prefetch. If microcalls are hitting different conversation keys (per-event keys), they won't reuse the KV.

- Aggregation options: We offer two ways to reduce quantum impact on microcalls:
  1) Client-side batching: SDK helper to coalesce very short microcalls for a short window (200ms) before sending.
  2) Server-side microcall aggregation policy: Redwood aggregates microcalls within a customer endpoint for billing purposes if they are below an X-token threshold and within a Y-second window. That aggregation is a billing-only aggregation and does not change runtime behavior.

- Edge case: Streaming answers (server->client token streaming) are billed at the full token count produced — rounding still applies per call.

Markus — if we offer cache TTL extension + pilot concession (2 months at 8-token quantum for microcalls) and a one-page calc in the SOW, I think finance will be satisfied. Beth — does that match what you need to present to your CFO?

— Kimberly
